test_title: SSC CGL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 2 March 2023)
subject: general
question: 40 litres of milk are kept in a container. 4 litres of milk were removed from this container and replaced with water. This procedure was performed two more times. How much milk does the container now hold?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total quantity (x) = 40 litres, quantity replaced (y) = 4 litres, total operations (n) = 3.

Remaining milk = x × (1 − y/x)ⁿ

Remaining milk = 40 × (1 − 4/40)³ = 40 × (9/10)³

Remaining milk = 40 × 0.729 = 29.16 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 29.16 litres.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Initial amount of milk = 40 litres

Amount removed and replaced by water = 4 litres

Total number of times the process is performed = 1 (initially) + 2 (more) = 3 times

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/939c49c25063f8c5ad2599123e1f6600a94b41a5a54e872418a609568e8c09a5.png] 

Formula Used:

Final Quantity = Initial Quantity × (1 − Replaced Quantity / Total Quantity)Time

Calculations:

⇒ Quantity of milk after 1st replacement = 40 − 4 = 36 litres

⇒ Ratio of milk remaining after each replacement = (40 − 4) ÷ 40 = 36/40 = 9/10

⇒ Milk left after 3 operations = 40 × (9/10) × (9/10) × (9/10)

⇒ Milk left = 40 × (729 / 1000)

⇒ Milk left = 4 × 72.9 / 10

⇒ Milk left = 291.6 / 10 = 29.16 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 29.16 litres.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Replacement Formula

Amount of pure liquid left = P × (1 − R/P)ⁿ, where P is initial quantity, R is quantity replaced, and n is number of cycles.

Ratio of Ingredients

The ratio of the original liquid to the replacing liquid (water) after n operations is [P × (1 − R/P)ⁿ] : [P − (P × (1 − R/P)ⁿ)].

Percentage Purity

Final concentration percentage = (Initial concentration) × (1 − R/P)ⁿ.</p
